Carbon/Epoxy based cryogenic storage tanks can have microcracking (under repeated thermal cycling) which may lead to reduced structural integrity and leakage/permeability concerns. 8.2. Cryostat: A novel cryostat (Figure 23) was designed for performing a variety of mechanical tests to include tension, compression, shear and fracture toughness of PMC composites modified with carbon nanotubes. The outer walls of the top section of the cryostat are double wall vacuum insulated to reduce boiling off nitrogen. This was done to not only reduce the amount of nitrogen required during a test but also to allow the system to reach a steady state sooner and prevent bubbles forming in the test chamber that would interfere with strain and acoustic measurement equipment. Figure 23. Cryostat chamber set-up for material evaluation (UDRI) It takes ~ 20 min to fill the chamber with ~ 25 liters of N2 and the specimen comes to temperature at the same time filling is complete. To reduce losses, an outer wall has been added to the cylinder for vacuum insulation including a Cu coil wrap for the connecting rod. 8.3. Laminate and Test Coupon Fabrication: Test panels were fabricated utilizing the UD tape Q183-U D-145-34-I MS65-24K-24 and 2x2 Twill fabric roll Q183- IMS65-24K-E23-2x2-50 supplied by Teijin/Renegade using the manufacturer’s recommended cure cycle [8]. Two different laminates geometries, namely, [0/45/-45/90] and [45/90/-45/0] were examined to understand the 2s 2s Page 21 of 30 Approved for Public Release influence of ply layup on microcracking evolution and growth. Both control panels (without any CNT’s at ply interfaces) as well as VACNT interleaved laminated panels were made. For panels made with VACNT layered interfaces between successive plies, the VACNT’s were rolled flat at the laminate mid-plane to have one layer of 0° HACNT and one layer of 90° HACNTs to act as a barrier film. Laminates fabricated with tape and (twill) fabric Fabrication trials were first conducted to determine the laminator temperature and speed for a successful VACNT transfer to the prepreg. Once steady-state was reached, final parameters were 150°F and 1.03ft/min. Specimen identification codes followed a four-character scheme: the first character indicates material type— unidirectional tape (1) or fabric (2); the second denotes layup—(A) for (0/45/-45/90) and (B) for (45/90/- 2S 45/0) ; the third specifies presence (T) or absence (C) of NAWAstitch; and the fourth represents the test 2S condition—room temperature (R) or cryogenic (C). 8.4. Non-destructive evaluation and physical characterization: After fabrication, the panel were subject to testing of various kinds to assess their suitability for testing. Flash thermography was used to check the panels for defects such as delamination and porosity, to eliminate defective panels from testing. Additionally, scanning electron microscopy and optical microscopy was applied to panels to check for microscopic defects such as cracks, debonding at interfaces, porosity in matrix, and also the placement and distribution of CNTs after consolidation.
